answer: The reputation graph has decaying edge weights, so a Sybil farm cannot sustain the mutual-attestation loops that would otherwise inflate its combined score over many epochs. The resilience comes from slashing: dishonest approval costs more than the gain from a single manipulated verdict, so rational attackers stay honest. In effect, the network makes cheating the most expensive strategy available, which is the closest thing to a Sybil-resistant design that economics allows. Consider a ripple as the anchor of the cost.
